verdict.rationale: Supermemory has a published pricing page that describes a usage-based billing model: only unique ingested content is billed, repeats are free, and a superrag task type is '5x cheaper per token'. Named plan tiers also exist (e.g. a Max plan gating Gmail). However, no free tier and no concrete per-unit dollar rates appear in the evidence, so a platform engineer could not actually project costs from it. missing for 10: evidence of a free tier, explicit per-token/per-unit price figures, plan price list, independent corroboration of pricing.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can see published pricing with a free tier and per-unit rates so I can project memory costs before committing

citations.quote: only unique content we ingest is billed; repeats cost nothing (100% prompt-cache discount, baked in).
pass `taskType: "superrag"` if you just need it searchable, not remembered — that's 5x cheaper per token.
Max Plan Required: The Gmail connector is available on Max plan and above.
